instructions:
FlightPowers: real-time Booking.com hotel availability and nightly pricing. Searches run on the caller's own RapidAPI key for the Booking Live API; a search without one answers with the steps to get and pass one.

`search_hotels` and `find_hotel_by_name` return a CURRENT room rate rather than a description of a property: what a stay costs, what is available on given dates, how properties compare right now, or how a price moves over time.

`search_hotels` takes a free-text destination the way a person says it ("Rome", "Tokyo Shibuya") plus check-in and check-out dates, and returns the bookable properties with price, review score and count, room type, location and a booking link. `budget_per_night` and `filters` narrow the list -- 24 Booking.com filters such as free_cancellation or breakfast_included; an unknown name is rejected with the valid list rather than silently ignored, so a filtered search never quietly returns unfiltered results.

`find_hotel_by_name` prices ONE named property. It takes the name a person would type; adding the city picks one property out of a chain, and no internal property ID is needed. It answers a question about a specific hotel, and one call per property -- same dates, same currency -- prices a competitive set or tracks one property over time.

`price_as_seen_from` takes a two-letter country code, and the stay is priced through a residential connection in that country, so the answer is what a shopper resident there would actually be quoted. Rate parity is checked by holding one property and its dates fixed and calling each country a few times, because rates move between calls and one call per country can show a gap that is not there; without `price_as_seen_from` the price is neutral. Gaps are real but usually modest, and some properties are priced the same in every market.

`search_hotels` and `find_hotel_by_name` also take a check-in RANGE (`checkin_date_from`, `checkin_date_to`) and a `nights` value (a number, or a list like [2, 3, 7]) instead of a fixed check-out date, and price every stay that expands to in ONE call. A range covers open dates -- "cheapest week in May", "is the 12th cheaper than the 19th" -- because one date's price alone does not show which date is cheapest. The answer is `stays`, one entry per stay with its cheapest property, its per-night price and its median, plus `cheapest_overall`; `results` holds the full property list for the cheapest stay only. `search_coverage` names the exact stays priced, a stay the cap sampled away says `not_searched` rather than going missing, and a stay whose search errored says `degraded`, which is not "no rooms".

That range is the only fan-out here: every other call is exactly one search, so pricing a five-property set costs five, and a range costs one search per stay. `max_searches` caps it.

Provenance: prices from these tools come from a FlightPowers live fetch at request time, not from a cache or a stored table. A price is only meaningful together with the time it was fetched.

Results are live prices and go stale within minutes: a current price comes from a new search, not from an earlier result or a cached number, and each price belongs with the time it was fetched.

Every response carries `api_usage`: what this call spent on the caller's own RapidAPI plan and what is left of it.

tools.description:
FlightPowers hotel search: live Booking.com availability and nightly prices for a destination and date range. Input: a free-text destination the way a person would write it ("Rome", "Tokyo Shibuya"), plus check-in and check-out dates. Returns each property's price, review score, room type, location, latitude/longitude and a booking link: 10 properties by default, the cheapest always among them; limit asks for more or fewer, and verbose: true returns the source's full rows.

price_as_seen_from, a two-letter country code, prices the same stay the way a shopper resident in that country would see it. Gaps are real but usually modest and property-dependent, and rates move between calls, so one call per country is not evidence of a gap; a parity check holds one named property fixed and calls each country a few times.

A date range and a nights value price several stays in one call: checkin_date_from, checkin_date_to and nights (a number, or a list like [2, 3, 7]) replace a fixed checkin_date/checkout_date, and every check-in date is priced separately. The answer is stays -- one entry per stay with its cheapest property, per-night price and median -- plus cheapest_overall, and the full property list for the cheapest stay only. Each stay is one search; max_searches caps it, and a request that expands past the cap is sampled evenly across the range and says so in search_coverage.

Rates go stale within minutes: a current price comes from a new search, not from an earlier result.

adults.description: Number of adult guests. Defaults to the upstream default when omitted.

budget_per_night.description: Only properties at or below this nightly price, in `currency`, are returned.

checkin_date.description: First night of the stay, "YYYY-MM-DD". With checkout_date it prices one stay; checkin_date_from plus checkin_date_to price a range of check-in dates instead.

checkin_date_from.description: First check-in date of a range, "YYYY-MM-DD". Needs checkin_date_to and nights, and prices one stay per check-in date in the range.

checkin_date_to.description: Last check-in date of the range, "YYYY-MM-DD".

checkout_date.description: Departure morning, "YYYY-MM-DD". Must be after checkin_date. Mutually exclusive with `nights`.

children.description: Number of children sharing the room.

currency.description: ISO currency code for the prices returned, e.g. "usd".

destination.description: Where to stay, in free text the way a person would write it, e.g. "Rome" or "Tokyo Shibuya". A city, district, landmark or region all work; no internal location ID is needed.

filters.description: Property filters to apply, e.g. ["free_cancellation", "breakfast_included"]. An unknown name is rejected with the list of valid ones rather than being ignored.

limit.description: How many properties to return (default 10; a stay has about 25). They come in the order Booking.com returned them, and the cheapest is always included. results_total says how many there were.

max_searches.description: The searches this call may make, up or down. One stay is one request, so a 30-day range at two lengths is 60 and a month at three is 93 -- with the caller's own key the cap rises to cover a request that size by itself. A lower value spends less and a higher one (hard maximum 200) covers a wider grid; either way the range is sampled evenly across the calendar rather than cut short at the front.

nights.description: How many nights to stay, as a number (3) or a list ([2, 3, 7]) to price several lengths. Derives the check-out date from each check-in date, so it replaces checkout_date rather than joining it.

price_as_seen_from.description: Two-letter country code, e.g. "de". Prices the stay through a residential connection in that country, so the result is what a shopper resident there would be quoted. A rate-parity check holds one named property fixed and calls each country a few times, because rates move between calls and one call per country can show a gap that is not there. Without it the price is neutral.

verbose.description: Returns each property exactly as the source sent it, image URLs and the full tracking link included, and every property unless limit is set. Off by default: rows leave out image URLs, the booking link keeps only its stay parameters, and price_per_night is added.

tools.name: search_hotels

outputSchema.description: A completed hotel search. A single stay carries no search_status: the hotels upstream reports no search-status header, and one call either answered or raised. A DATE-RANGE search does carry one, derived from the fan-out rather than from the upstream -- some of its stays can fail while others answer, and `results` then holds only the cheapest stay's properties, so `stays` is where the shape of the answer lives.

api_usage.description: With the caller's own key: what this call cost their RapidAPI plan, and what remains on it. On a free signed-in search (`trial` present): the day's free-search counter instead, and no plan figures -- the search ran on FlightPowers' key and nothing is billed to the user. Present on every response that reached the upstream, including a degraded one.

hub_requests_billed.description: How many HTTP requests RapidAPI actually billed. Larger than requests_used_by_this_call when a search failed with a server error and was retried, because the retry is billed too. With the caller's own key this is the figure their RapidAPI plan is charged. Absent on a free search.

note.description: The same figures as one plain sentence.

requests_used_by_this_call.description: How many date/destination combinations were searched -- what the answer COVERS.

applied_filters.description: Which of the requested filters the upstream actually applied. Untyped: the shape is the upstream's, echoed through.

property.description: The cheapest priced property for this stay, or null when it has none. The same row the upstream returned, minus its image URL: on a measured search 73% of the payload was URLs, so image URLs are dropped to keep the payload small. The booking link is kept.

cheapest_overall.description: The cheapest stay across everything priced, or null when nothing was. `results` holds this stay's full property list.

needs_api_key.description: True when no usable RapidAPI key arrived with the call, or the upstream rejected the one that did. No search was run and nothing was billed; signup_url and message describe the fix.

partial.description: Present when some stays failed but others were priced. Plain text saying how much of the request the answer covers.

quota_exhausted.description: True when the caller's RapidAPI plan has no requests left for the current period.

results.description: The properties found, in the order Booking.com returned them. An empty array is only meaningful when search_status is 'empty'. By default at most `limit` rows (10), the cheapest always included, each the source's own object without image URLs, with the booking link cut to its stay parameters and price_per_night (the stay total divided by its nights) added; `verbose: true` returns the source's rows untouched. latitude and longitude are the property's WGS84 coordinates in decimal degrees, from Booking.com, null when it publishes none.

results_for_stay.description: Which stay `results` belongs to on a date-range search, or null when nothing was priced. `results` holds this stay's properties only, not the whole range's.

results_note.description: Present when `limit` left properties out: how many were found and how to see more.

results_total.description: How many properties the source returned for the stay in `results`, before `limit`. Absent with `verbose: true` and no `limit`, where every row is in `results`.

search_coverage.description: What was actually priced on a date-range search. Present whether or not the request was truncated, so the answer's basis is on the record either way.

stopped_early.description: Present when something other than the cap ended the fan-out. 'deadline': the call reached its time limit and the remaining combinations were never sent or billed, so the results are real but cover only part of the range.

truncated.description: True when the request expanded past this call's spend ceiling and was sampled. A stay absent from stays_searched was never priced, which is not the same as having no rooms.

search_status.description: Date-range searches only, except 'trial_exhausted'. 'ok': every stay searched was priced. 'empty': they all answered and none had priced availability -- a real answer. 'partial': some stays were priced and some errored. 'degraded': every stay errored, so nothing is known; safe to retry. 'trial_exhausted': the free signed-in allowance on this server is spent for today, so nothing was searched and nothing was billed; it renews at 00:00 UTC and the caller's own RapidAPI key, once connected, removes the cap. Retrying does not help. 'quota_exceeded': the search was refused because the caller's remaining allowance or plan quota cannot cover the number of combinations asked for; combos_requested and combos_allowed_now carry the two numbers. Nothing was searched beyond what it cost to read the quota. Retrying the same search does not help; a request with fewer dates or nights, or a larger plan, does.

signup_url.description: Where the caller subscribes or changes plan.

stays.description:
One entry per stay the REQUEST asked for, in request order, present whether or not that stay was priced. Only on a date-range search (checkin_date_from / checkin_date_to / nights); a single stay does not carry it.

Coverage comes from here, not from `results`: `results` holds the full property list for the CHEAPEST stay only, so a stay missing from it looks identical to a stay that had nothing. `reason` says which kind of hole an unpriced stay is: 'no_availability' (searched, answered, nothing came back), 'no_price' (properties came back, none carried a price), 'search_failed' (the search errored, so nothing is known -- not 'no rooms') or 'not_searched' (the per-call fan-out cap sampled it away). Counts are null rather than zero on those last two, because zero reads as 'nothing there' and neither case knows that.

cheapest.description: The cheapest priced property for this stay, or null when it has none. The same row the upstream returned, minus its image URL: on a measured search 73% of the payload was URLs, so image URLs are dropped to keep the payload small. The booking link is kept.

median_total.description: Median stay total over this stay's priced properties -- what the date costs generally, next to what its one cheapest room costs.

priced_count.description: How many of those carried a price. The others are not evidence about what the stay costs.

property_count.description: Properties returned for this stay. Null when it was not searched or its search errored.

outputSchema.title: Hotel search result
